editor.edits:
Two correctness fixes, both high confidence, and one cleanup. Committed as ba2b2ec.

1. **A failing criterion did not flag the delivery.** The writer had `flagged: !exitGate`, and `exitGate` depends only on `tests.passed && mvi_verdict`. So an editor that returned a `fail` verdict alongside `mvi_verdict: true` would ship the unit unflagged, and criterion 3 depended entirely on the model obeying its prompt. It is now `flagged: !exitGate || failedCriteria.length > 0 || ungradedCriteria > 0`. `ungradedCriteria = unitCriteria(unit).length - criteriaVerdicts.length`, so an editor that silently skips criteria also ships flagged, with a log line saying so. A Python source test pins both.

2. **The no-criteria editor prompt changed more than the criterion allows.** The writer added `(no acceptance criteria were supplied — this run had no --spec pointer). Leave criteria_verdicts empty.` and re-wrapped the line. Criterion 2 allows only the one "leave empty" sentence. I cut the parenthetical, so the line now reads `the title "T". Leave criteria_verdicts empty. This can overturn the writer's claim.` I diffed the zero-criteria prompts against c03734a: the writer prompt is IDENTICAL, and the editor prompt differs only by that sentence. I updated the JS test to assert the exact line.

3. **The writer's code and test comments are removed**, per the repo's "Agents write zero comments in code, including tests" rule, and its multi-line test-class docstring is cut to one line to match the sibling classes. The pre-existing trailing comment on the `flagged:` line also went, because that line's meaning changed. No behavior was lost.

Kept as they were: `unitCriteria` (one shared filter for both prompts, tested), the `loadFunction` deps helper (needed to test the prompts against the real source), and the editor-off log suffix.

Both suites are green and print no warnings: pytest 13 passed, node 11 passed.

I kept it: it stops a path with a quote or similar character from breaking out of the git -C quoting that the workflow writes into agent instructions. Mutation check: removing --path-format=absolute makes 3 tests fail. The suite also passes under -W error (37 passed). Handoff written to .studio/output/impl_loop/work_dir_validation/impl--work_dir_validation--editor.json.

criteria_verdicts.criterion: A path that does not exist stops the run before the loop, naming that reason.
criteria_verdicts.evidence: test_validate_work_dir_rejects_a_path_that_does_not_exist and test_cli_bad_work_dir_raises_before_any_knobs_are_emitted pass. Running the CLI by hand printed 'work-dir missing: no directory at /nonexistent-xyz' and exited 1. forge.md Step 3 stops on a non-zero exit before Step 5 runs the loop.

criteria_verdicts.criterion: A path that exists but is not a git worktree stops the run, naming that reason.
criteria_verdicts.evidence: These tests pass: test_validate_work_dir_rejects_a_directory_that_is_not_a_worktree, the two cases of test_validate_work_dir_rejects_a_path_inside_a_worktree_that_is_not_its_top (sub and .git), and test_validate_work_dir_calls_an_existing_file_not_a_worktree. Running the CLI on /tmp printed 'work-dir not-a-worktree: /private/tmp is not the top level of a git worktree' and exited 1.

criteria_verdicts.criterion: A worktree belonging to a different repository stops the run, naming that reason.
criteria_verdicts.evidence: test_validate_work_dir_rejects_a_worktree_of_another_repository passes. It uses a real git worktree of a second repository. validate_work_dir in studio/impl_loop.py compares the two common git dirs and raises with the different-repo reason.

criteria_verdicts.criterion: The same-repo check compares `--git-common-dir` using `--path-format=absolute`, proven by a test that fails when the flag is removed.
criteria_verdicts.evidence: I removed --path-format=absolute from studio/impl_loop.py:210 with sed and reran the suite. Three tests failed: test_git_common_dir_uses_the_absolute_path_format, test_validate_work_dir_accepts_a_worktree_of_this_repo and test_cli_work_dir_flag_reports_the_resolved_path. After restoring the flag, all 37 passed.

criteria_verdicts.criterion: With a work dir set, `/forge` resolves `scriptPath` into that directory rather than the main repo.
criteria_verdicts.evidence: This lives only in the /forge instructions, so no test can check it. I read .claude/commands/forge.md:216: with --work-dir, scriptPath is <work_dir>/.claude/workflows/implementation-loop.js. The Workflow call also passes work_dir in args, and the workflow uses it in gitIn and workDirPreamble (implementation-loop.js:56-66).

criteria_verdicts.criterion: With a work dir set, Step 3's branch selection and dirty-tree check report on the work dir, not the current directory.
criteria_verdicts.evidence: This lives only in the /forge instructions, so no test can check it. I read .claude/commands/forge.md:140-152: rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD and status --porcelain both run with git -C "<work_dir>". The branch is checked out or created in the work directory, and the dirty-tree stop tells the user to commit or stash in the work directory.
